# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, common base
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies, build LAMMPS with REAXFF, and clean up in a single layer
# This approach minimizes image size in a single-stage build.
RUN apt-get update && \
    # Install build-time and run-time dependencies
    # ca-certificates: for secure network communication (e.g., git clone)
    # git, build-essential, cmake, python3: for compiling the source code. Python3 is required by CMake.
    # openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: for MPI support
    # libgomp1: required OpenMP runtime library
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates \
        git \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        python3 \
        openmpi-bin \
        libopenmpi-dev \
        libgomp1 && \
    #
    # Clone the latest (default) branch of the LAMMPS repository as per corrected instructions
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /opt/lammps && \
    cd /opt/lammps && \
    #
    # Configure and build LAMMPS using CMake
    # -D PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package required for the simulation
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
        ../cmake && \
    #
    # Compile using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    #
    # Copy the main LAMMPS executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp lmp /usr/local/bin/ && \
    #
    # Set up the working directory and copy example files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    #
    # Clean up build dependencies and source code to reduce final image size
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/lammps && \
    apt-get purge -y git build-essential cmake python3 libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# For MPI applications in containers, it's often necessary to specify network interfaces at runtime.
# Example for Open MPI with mpirun:
# mpirun -np 4 --mca btl_tcp_if_exclude lo,docker0 lmp -in in.hns
# The ENTRYPOINT is set to the LAMMPS executable so users can pass arguments directly.
ENTRYPOINT ["lmp"]

# Default command to run if no other command is provided
CMD ["--help"]

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 3 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: false
    runFlux: true
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 48

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment
# within the Flux Framework on a Kubernetes cluster.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reax-minicluster
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods to create for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The number of MPI tasks to run. The command will be wrapped in `flux run -n <tasks> ...`
  tasks: 1

  # Defines the container that will run the Flux-managed job.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by Flux.
      # The operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks>` to this command.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # launcher is false, meaning this container will host the flux broker and workers,
      # not just submit a job to a separate cluster.
      launcher: false
      # runFlux is true, indicating that the Flux broker should be started within this container.
      # This is the standard for non-launcher, single-container MiniClusters.
      runFlux: true

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods after the job completes.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

updates.reason: The previous FOM of 9.289 is very low, suggesting a serial or under-scaled run. This attempt targets a 64-core HPC-optimized ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scales the LAMMPS job to run in parallel across all 64 cores (4x4x4 decomposition). This is expected to yield a significant performance improvement.

The prior 64-core ARM run achieved a strong FOM (329). This attempt targets a 48-core AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge) to test if higher per-core performance on a modern x86 CPU can surpass the previous result.

The peak performance of 329.285 was achieved on the 64-core hpc7g.16xlarge instance. The subsequent run on a 48-core AMD instance resulted in a lower FOM of 272.891. This indicates that the higher core count and architecture of the Graviton3 HPC instance are optimal for this workload among the available choices. The optimization is considered complete.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 4 -v y 4 -v z 3 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: false
    runFlux: true
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 48

context.details: Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH. You MUST install libgomp1.

context.optimize:
Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x X -v y Y -v z Z -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite      
You MUST choose (and change) parameters for X Y Z and instance type and resources that will maximize the FOM, the M-atom or k-atom steps per second.
